title: Officer cleared in fatal shooting
article: A Peel Regional Police officer will not face criminal charges for shooting to death a Port Credit man who tried to attack him with two knives, the Province's Special Investigations Unit announced today.

SIU director Ian Scott said there are "no reasonable grounds" to believe the Peel officer committed a criminal offence in relation to the death of Gregory Moynagh, 25, who was bipolar and for years battled mental illness.
The SIU probe determined that in the early hours last Dec. 21, three Peel officers went to an apartment on Helene St. in Port Credit in response to a disturbance call.
One officer went to speak with the person who had reported the disturbance, while the other two contacted Moynagh and had a conversation with him behind a closed apartment door, the SIU said.
Moynagh told the officers that he was armed with knives, at which point both officers drew their guns and backed away from the apartment door, the SIU said.
Moynagh then opened the door and confronted the officers. He had a serrated knife in each hand with the blades pointing up, the SIU said.

One of the officers backed away towards a stairwell and the other officer backed up as well, both shouting at Moynagh to drop the knives. Instead, Moynagh approached one of the officers and was within four feet of him when he lunged at the officer, knives in hand, the SIU probe determined.
The officer shot Moynagh twice. He died at the scene.
"In my view, the subject officer had the right to use lethal force under...the Criminal Code because he believed on reasonable grounds that it was necessary for his self-preservation...," Scott said.
In the days prior to the shooting, Moynagh had complained that new medication he was on was "making him crazy," his girlfriend, Brittani Silvestre, said.
Michelle Burry said Moynagh, whom she described as a good friend, was a caring man who did a lot for friends and family.
